title: Love it with a few caveats
body:
I really like this app for the most part, and I haven’t found another one that doesn’t jump to the next task automatically. You must check off that the task is done before it starts the timer for the next task, which is great because if you get behind on the apps that automate the task jumping, all of a sudden you’re 3 tasks behind and the routine becomes useless. This also gives you the anticipated time of completion, which is a helpful and rare feature. However, there are a few things that bug me. When I’m trying to rearrange tasks, the app doesn’t scroll up as I’m dragging, so I have to drop the task, scroll down, and then move it again, which is annoying since I have long routines with lots of tasks. 

I also wish there was an option to see all the steps at once while I’m in routine mode (sort of like on google maps where you can check the route overview without stopping the directions). If I run over on one task and realize I’m going to be late, I’d like to quickly check which tasks are coming up and decide which ones I can skip or adjust without stopping the timer. 

The "do later" feature is useful, but it seems to move the task to the end of the list permanently, which I don’t want. I’d prefer it to just temporarily move the task.

Lastly, I don’t think there needs to be a save button. Changes should save automatically, and having to hit "save" just adds an unnecessary step with no benefit. If I make a change, it should be saved right away so I don’t risk losing the input.

But then after you’ve got it set up, you find yourself overwhelmed every time you open it and see all the categories of things you’re supposed to do that day. All the routines. Well, anyway, that’s been the case for me. I think most of the people who benefit from this type of app really need the least amount of overwhelm possible. While this app solves it inside of a routine, it doesn’t solve it when you’re selecting a routine.

This is a perfect app and I love how detailed some of the preset tasks are, and it’s also very simple. author: Maria LZB

title: Thrilled to find this.
body:
I’ve been trying to find an app for years that can help remind me to do stuff. After a week I start to ignore the reminders no matter how much I want to get things done. The routines have made it easier for me to manage lots of multi-task things with significantly less anxiety. Just getting up and doing a basic morning routine would have me paralyzed. Since I started using your app I love that it tells me my morning routine only takes “28 minutes” to me that has significantly helped my fawn response. My brain can handle doing something for 28 minutes. Where before is see this list of things and just immediately want to hide and not know where to start. I’ve only been using it 3 weeks and it’s already doing great things! 

I also love the simplicity and that there aren’t a lot of things to make me distracted. I love the idea of Finch and some of the others but I lose myself in all the details. 

Also agree with other review thanks for the forever option for the fee. I don’t mind paying for apps but I don’t like doing it monthly and for something life changing like this and so necessary it makes it more accessible.
author: Atwistedlime

title: Flexible and Helpful
body: This is the only checklist type app type I have found that is both flexible enough AND gives structure and examples. The interface is simple and attractive. I’m actually focusing on things that I’ve struggled with for years and am making better habits.
author: Wazeandmeans

title: Seems promising for regulating ADHD
body:
First off, thank you for offering a lifetime purchase, simply fantastic as I can’t afford to pay subs for dozens of apps. 

I really like the idea of this and I hope it will help regulate my ADHD. I LOVE that the app isn’t over designed and bloated with a ton of buttons, sub menus, extra fluff that is hard to figure out and navigate as an easily distracted person, lol. I’ve tried apps like Stoic and Finch, and the amount of content they have always confused and pushed me away. So thank you for designing something easy to use and understand immediately. 

I hope in any future updates, this app doesn’t become a bloated mess. Don’t fix what isn’t broke!
author: stephastro

author: kangwc

title: 30 Days Changed!
body: I’ve been using this for 30 days and it has truly changed my life! At the end of 2022 I was at a breaking point and absolutely pushing so many tasks “under the rug”.  This has given me the motivation and accountability I need to get things done. It’s so simple but being able to see my progress and the number of days I’ve accomplished certain tasks has given me confidence in what I’m doing. It has helped me stay on top of business, personal, and household tasks. Forever grateful for routine flow!
author: Mackenziejoan

title: This is a very helpful app!
body:
It helps you keep on track in your day! Very user friendly app. Love it! 

It might not be perfect, but people this app is very new, it was released only 4 months ago… give it the chance to be improved. 

My husband is a mobile developer here in USA and I know for a fact that the most insignificant mistake can cause an app to fail. That is why an early user gets the lifetime price deal, because you have to bear with with some minor situations in the beginning. 

But overall!! I love this app!!

author: The Real Tampa Turtle

title: SO MUCH POTENTIAL. [But funny glitch.]
body:
[I’ve taken my time, only putting in a few simple routines to try it out to see how it would work. The last update deleted my first two routines. This last update restored them but deleted my two new ones I input. Maybe we can get a handle on that. 😅]
I’m really excited to be one of the first users of this app before it blows up. It’s very close to something I wanted to build a couple years ago, but I’m not really a programmer and got stuck—it was just too much for me at the time. I’m absolutely stoked that someone else has done it, and if the writer ever looks for a team I would love to be on it.
